rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Followers cannot excuse evil by blaming oppressive leaders: each person answers for himself and must proclaim truth under pressure, trusting God even if this brings martyrdom.
rows.anchor: Each person is responsible for his own self; he cannot put this responsibility on others and absolve himself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term for the defiant leaders means people who regard themselves as high-status or are intoxicated by that status; leadership that diverts people from God is arrogance and ends in Hell for leaders and followers.
rows.anchor: people who thought themselves to be of high status or who were inebriated with their high status

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in Hell ask its keepers to request one day of relief; the keepers point out that messengers had brought clear signs and tell them to petition God themselves.
rows.anchor: the guards of Hell to request God to lessen the punishment just for one day so that they can have some reprieve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned have no recourse: neither their deities nor leaders help them, and God does not heed their calls; every door of hope is closed.
rows.anchor: these leaders prove to be of any help to them nor will God listen to them. All doors of hope shall stand closed on them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 51 returns to verse 45 after an intervening account of the punishment awaiting Pharaoh and his followers: God helps messengers and believers in this world and on the Day of Judgement.
rows.anchor: The Almighty says in this verse that just as He helped Moses (sws) and the true believer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier exegetes are confused because they fail to distinguish prophet from messenger; God’s established practice toward messengers is to establish a court of justice against their rejecters in this world, who are destroyed by calamity or believers’ force, during or after the messenger’s life.
rows.anchor: The reason for this is that they are not fully aware of the difference between a nabī (prophet) and a rasūl (messenger).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of the witnesses is Judgement: prophets and messengers testify to their teaching, communities answer for their response, and angels bring the record of deeds.
rows.anchor: on that Day the Almighty will ask each prophet and messenger to bear witness to what they taught their people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 52 explains the previous verse’s Day: clear testimony defeats every excuse, including blaming leaders for leading followers astray.
rows.anchor: such will be the clarity and certainty of the evidence borne by witnesses produced in the divine court on that Day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders will deny responsibility and say their followers knew they were astray; both groups are equally liable, and their excuse earns God’s and the angels’ curse and an evil abode.
rows.anchor: their followers deserve this fate because they full well knew that their leaders had gone astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment of Pharaoh’s party and the guidance and Book given to Moses and believing Israelites illustrate God’s help to messengers and believers.
rows.anchor: while Moses (sws) and the Israelites who professed belief in him were bestowed with guidance and the Book of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book embodies the promise of worldly supremacy and sovereignty; Israelites retained supremacy while they adhered to it.
rows.anchor: Thus the Israelites were supreme as long as they adhered to this Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book guides people to God and reminds them of His directives, but benefits only those with insight; the remark is sarcastic toward Israelites who foolishly turned from its light.
rows.anchor: only those people who have vision and intellect will benefit from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 55 summarizes the argument and reassures Muhammad to continue preaching: the promise of success for messengers and their followers in this world and the Hereafter is certain.
rows.anchor: He is asked to adhere to his preaching; God’s promise is certain to materialize.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness and glorifying God with praise morning and evening are the method for acquiring the patience required for the promise to materialize.
rows.anchor: the methodology to acquire the patience which is an essential condition for this promise to materialize.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and seeking forgiveness cultivate patience; the address is to Muhammad as representative of his people, so its attribution of sin should be read in that context.
rows.anchor: the way to acquire patience is to offer the prayer and to seek forgiveness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing section urges Muhammad to persevere, promises help and victory, threatens Quraysh with punishment in both worlds, and interweaves arguments for monotheism and the Hereafter from moral, inner, and outer experience.
rows.anchor: these verses besides urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and perseverance also give him glad tidings of help and victory

none: Publisher footer fragment only; no source discussion is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s central theme is monotheism, with Judgement underscoring its force: each person faces the all-powerful God, and no one can rescue another or speak without His leave.
rows.anchor: The central theme of this sūrah also is monotheism. In deference to this central theme, a warning has also been sounded about the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah argues from prophetic history: all prophets called to monotheism and received divine revelation; religious divisions arose from enmity, envy, stubbornness, and imagined superiority after truth was revealed.
rows.anchor: all prophets from Adam (sws) and Noah (sws) called people to this very religion of monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the measure of truth, and if people reject its verdict, the scale of Judgement will decide their dispute.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān has been revealed as a barometer and scale for the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah came late in the Makkan period before migration; its address bids Quraysh farewell after the Prophet fulfilled his duty, while Muslims enter a collective phase of responsibility.
rows.anchor: it was revealed at the end of the Makkan period right before migration to Madīnah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to present truth clearly, not force faith; he should leave the opponents’ fate to God, while the sūrah answers objections to his prophethood.
rows.anchor: his responsibility was to clearly present the truth before the people which he has fulfilled

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening section presents the Qur’an’s revelation as continuous with earlier revelation, exalts God’s sovereignty, and says Muhammad must warn Makkah of Judgement; he is not responsible for opponents’ faith, and only the worthy are guided.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is addressed and informed that the very religion of monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates, provides, and grants children; all prophets taught one religion, and sectarian division after knowledge arose from enmity and prejudice. Muhammad must preach it and use the revealed Book as a just scale; opponents face punishment, while delay reflects God’s practice of granting respite.
rows.anchor: Those who created differences in it did so after true knowledge had come to them from God and did so merely because of mutual enmity and prejudice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overview says invented partners and religion cannot help idolaters at Judgement, whereas believers who do good succeed; the Prophet’s concern for guidance arises from kinship rather than a demand for reward.
rows.anchor: if he is very concerned about their guidance, then it is not because he wants some reward from them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents call revelation fabricated, Muhammad knows God granted it and can end it; its effects—eradicating evil and raising truth—should satisfy him, as those worthy will accept the call.
rows.anchor: how through it, He is obliterating evil and elevating the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth does not prove right guidance; God limits provision to protect people from Satan’s trials, and respite is no license for rebellion. All depend on God, worldly gains pass, and believers who trust Him receive eternal dominion.
rows.anchor: Whatever disbelievers gain is temporary and transient.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ qualities and instructions prepare them for heightened opposition and their emergence as an organized community, so they can meet testing circumstances without missteps.
rows.anchor: the excesses committed by the disbelievers had greatly increased, and Muslims too were shaping up in the form of an organized group and community

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing passage warns opponents and invites them while there is still time; Muhammad must be patient if rejected because conveying the message, not forcing faith, is his duty. It also exposes human conceit after mercy and despair in hardship, denies divine partners, and explains revelation as God’s mode of speech.
rows.anchor: he has fulfilled the responsibility that was imposed on him; forcing down faith in their hearts is not his responsibility

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation given to Muhammad also reaches others through him; before it, he did not know the Book or the details of faith and its requirements.
rows.anchor: before this he was neither aware of the Book nor of the details of faith and its requirements

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic name Ḥā Mīm ‘Ayn Sīn Qāf shares the naming of the two preceding sūrahs, signaling shared central themes; its added letters indicate topics distinctive to this sūrah.
rows.anchor: Commonality in names bears witness to the commonality in central themes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika refers to the sūrah’s topics, whose name briefly signals them; the verse concisely says that God reveals to Muhammad as He revealed to earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: The overall message that is intended to be conveyed is something to the effect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika also signals unity of content and of revelation’s means: all prophets received the same teaching by the same method, so its content should not be strange or startling.
rows.anchor: the Almighty taught the same things to all the prophets and messengers as He is teaching Muḥammad (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad preached the same monotheistic religion as earlier prophets; idolaters and People of the Book opposed truth out of bias for invented religion.
rows.anchor: all the earlier prophets were deputed to preach

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God communicates with chosen prophets by revelation according to a fixed principle, not by appearing or speaking face-to-face to everyone; demands for such access are arrogance and foolishness.
rows.anchor: He has always stuck to this method that whomsoever He chooses as prophet He converses with him through revelations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion assures Muhammad and establishes the truth to opponents: he conveys the same revelation-based religion as earlier prophets, and his inability to make people see or hear God is no defect in his prophethood.
rows.anchor: Similarly, if the Prophet (sws) is not able to make people observe God or make others hear Him when He is speaking, then this also is no flaw of his prophethood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God mighty and wise reassures Muhammad and warns opponents: God can seize the arrogant, and any delay is respite granted in wisdom; Muhammad should trust God and consign their case to Him.
rows.anchor: if He does not catch them immediately then it is because He is granting them respite as per His wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns and controls everything in heaven and earth, has no associate or peer, and is exalted; giving respite or honoring someone does not put people beyond His control or entitle them to demand a direct encounter.
rows.anchor: Neither is anyone His associate in any matter nor is anything beyond His control or jurisdiction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens nearly split from God’s majesty, and angels near Him glorify and praise Him in fear while seeking forgiveness for earth’s inhabitants; idolaters wrongly expect angels to secure rank for their worshippers.
rows.anchor: the angels because of being so near to Him are glorifying and celebrating His praises all the time out of His fear

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ absolves God of evil and ḥamd affirms every good: they reject polytheism and affirm monotheism as God’s attributes.
rows.anchor: The former absolves God of all evil and the latter affirms every good in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ seeking forgiveness echoes the description of the throne-bearers and those around the Throne in Sūrah al-Mu’min.
rows.anchor: the following words of Sūrah al-Mu’min, the previous sūrah allude to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels seek forgiveness specifically for believers on earth; this is their intercession before God, not an independent power to forgive.
rows.anchor: This seeking of forgiveness of the angels is their intercession which they are doing for the believers in the presence of their Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God alone forgives and is merciful admonishes idolaters: if angels could forgive, they would not humbly ask God to do so.
rows.anchor: If this was in the jurisdiction of the angels, then why would they so earnestly and humbly request God to forgive people?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God watches those who take other protectors; when their allotted time expires His wrath seizes them. Muhammad must convey truth but is not accountable for their refusal.
rows.anchor: his responsibility was to communicate the truth to them which he is fulfilling and should keep on doing so as long as His Lord asks him to do so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika links this revelation to those sent before: God revealed an Arabic Qur’an to Muhammad to warn Makkah and its surroundings.
rows.anchor: in a similar manner the Almighty has sent down this Arabic Qur’ān to him so that he can inform people in the central city of Arabia and its whereabouts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier Arabic is intended to mark God’s favor and conclusively deliver the truth.
rows.anchor: to delineate the favour of God and to conclusively deliver the truth.
